title: Sukkaracan de Manpuku: The Secret Doctrine of the Kyoen Constitution — Economic Immunity Under the Duty-First Principle
abstract: This work presents the complete doctrine of 'economic immunity' — the structural capacity to remain independent from macroeconomic extraction — as derived from 16 years of first-person practice under the Duty-First Principle (義務先行説) of Tendo Economics (天道経済学). Central to the framework is the equation V = N/D, where V is realized value, N is the density of meaningful moral action, and D is friction and self-interest. As D approaches zero, V is liberated. title: The Human Prototype of AI Cognition: A 26-Year Question-Generation Process as a Case Study in Neural Architecture Design
abstract: We report a structural isomorphism between a 26-year human research process (2000–2026) and the functional architecture of modern neural language models. Key mapping: (1) adversarial experience = loss function signal; (2) narrative fragments = latent embeddings; (3) research questions = inference queries; (4) pre-prints = output validation; (5) Ma/間 (meaningful interval) = inference-time compute (chain-of-thought). We propose the Human Prototype of AI Cognition (HPAC) framework with 5 design principles and 4 application domains: autonomous research agent design, AI consciousness studies, educational system design, and independent researcher validation. Target journals: Nature Machine Intelligence / Minds and Machines / AI & Society.
keywords: AI cognition, neural architecture, question generation, HPAC framework, inference-time compute, Ma field, KOKU, chain-of-thought, loss function, latent embedding, autonomous research agent, 26 years, longitudinal, human prototype, machine consciousness, science of science

title: The Generative Structure of Interdisciplinary Research Questions: A Case Study of 166 Questions Across Six Domains Generated by a Single Researcher Over 26 Years (2000–2026)
abstract: This paper presents a structural analysis of how 166 research questions, spanning six academic domains (astrophysics, econophysics, behavioral economics, cognitive science, chronobiology, and theoretical physics), were generated by a single researcher over 26 years (2000–2026). Using a corpus of 197 narrative/philosophical fragments extracted from pre-print drafts, we identify three generative patterns: (A) adversarial experience → structural question, (B) somatic/perceptual event → theoretical question, (C) incidental observation → empirical question. Key findings: Language/Japanese (n=141, 71.6%) and Time/Interval (n=127, 64.5%) are the dominant generative themes. A structural transition from philosophical to falsifiable questions is identified at 2013 (Mt.Gox collapse). Pre-registration with DOI timestamps is proposed as a substitute for institutional validation in independent research. Target journals: Scientometrics / Science and Education / PLOS ONE (Science of Science track).
keywords: science of science, question generation, interdisciplinary, longitudinal case study, intellectual genealogy, pre-registration, Ma field, KOKU, Japanese language, independent researcher, scientometrics, 26 years, 166 questions

title: 発想の土壌 / The Generative Soil: Structural Analysis of How Stories Produced Questions — TheYKHC 2000–2026
abstract: A structural analysis showing how 197 poetic/narrative fragments (the 'soil') generated 166 marked research questions across 13 historical epochs (2000–2026). Key findings: (1) The two dominant generative themes are Language/Japanese (141 fragments) and Time/Ma (127 fragments) — the insight that Japanese language encodes physical quantities (Ki, Ma, Genki) underlies the entire corpus. (2) Three question-generation patterns identified: Suffering→Question, Bodily Sensation→Question, Chance Observation→Question. (3) The Mt.Gox experience (2013) was the pivotal turning point that converted philosophical questions into falsifiable hypotheses. (4) The 1986 visual experience (age 16) was the earliest seed — the dual-layer universe structure was felt before it was theorized. (5) Question density peaked on May 24, 2026 — the night before the CSS observation window. Companion documents: Fragments collection DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20359882 / Question timeline DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20359895.
keywords: generative soil, intellectual history, question genesis, TheYKHC, Japanese language, Ma field, KOKU, 16 years, pattern analysis, Mt.Gox, 1986 experience, 発想の土壌, 問いの起源

title: 問いの年表 / The Timeline of Questions: 2000–2026 — TheYKHC Research Questions in Chronological Order
abstract: A chronological archive of all 195 research questions from TheYKHC corpus, organized by the year each question first emerged. title: 間の断片集 (Fragments of Ma): Philosophical and Poetic Passages Removed from 119 Scientific Pre-Prints — TheYKHC 2000–2026
abstract: A collection of 213 philosophical, poetic, and narrative fragments extracted from the original drafts of 119 TheYKHC scientific pre-prints. These passages were removed during the peer-review rewriting process to achieve scientific neutrality, but represent the conceptual origin of the research questions. Organized in 9 chapters: I. Solitude and Departure (孤独と出発) — II. The Discovery of Ma (間という発見) — III. The Intersection of Cosmos and Economy — IV. Tendo as Philosophy (天道という思想) — V. System and Succession — VI. Daily Words (光の言葉) — VII. Civilization Design — VIII. Journals and Records — IX. Other Fragments. The scientific papers from which these were removed are archived at DOI range 10.5281/zenodo.20359009–20359376. This collection answers the question the papers do not ask: why did this person spend 16 years asking these questions?

title: TheYKHC Research Question Archive v2.0: 195 Questions × 3-Layer Peer Review Analysis (Miki Critique / Luna Rebuttal / Methodology Completion)
abstract: This document presents a 3-layer peer review analysis of all 195 research questions extracted from 119 TheYKHC preprints across 6 academic streams. Layer 1 (Miki Critique): Each question is subjected to the toughest peer-reviewer objections targeting methodology, sample size, confounders, and causal claims. Layer 2 (Luna Rebuttal): Full-force scientific defense with literature support, statistical safeguards, and falsification conditions. Layer 3 (Methodology Completion): Primary method, 2 alternative methods, expected quantitative result, falsification condition, paper status, and target journal. Stream A (Statistics/Quantitative Finance): 13 questions, all READY_TO_SUBMIT. Stream B (Astrophysics/Neutrino Astronomy): 21 questions, all READY_TO_SUBMIT. Stream C (Behavioral Economics): 20 questions, NEEDS_DATA. Stream D (Cognitive Science/AI): 30 questions, CONCEPTUAL_ONLY (prototype stage). Stream E (Medicine/Life Sciences): 30 questions, NEEDS_DATA. Stream F (Theoretical Physics): 81

title: TheYKHC Research Question Archive v1.0: Complete Index of 195 Research Questions from 119 Pre-Prints Across 6 Academic Streams
abstract: This document is the complete index of research questions extracted from all 119 TheYKHC preprints (DOI-registered, Zenodo). A total of 195 research questions are organized across 6 independent academic streams: (A) Statistics/Quantitative Finance, (B) High-Energy Astrophysics/Neutrino Astronomy, (C) Behavioral Economics/Economic Physics, (D) Cognitive Science/AI Systems Design, (E) Medicine/Life Sciences/Social Experiment, (F) Theoretical Physics/Cosmology. Each question can be answered independently. Answer methods will be appended progressively. All questions converge on a single central purpose: to demonstrate through 6 independent academic streams that a statistically significant correlation exists between IceCube astrophysical signals (phi2/KOKU) and human economic, cognitive, and biological activity. This is a living document and master research agenda for the TheYKHC program.
keywords: research questions, IceCube, KOKU, phi2 field, Ma field, Tendo Economics, neutrino astronomy, behavioral economics, theoretical physics, AI systems, TheYKHC, research agenda, convergence proof

title: Seven Unsolved Problems in V=N/D Civilization Design
abstract: This paper documents seven fundamental unsolved problems that emerge when attempting to implement V=N/D (Value = Service Density / Friction) as a national operating system. V=N/D proposes that individual and collective value is best measured not by quantity of money or labor hours, but by the density of service delivered relative to the friction generated. While the theoretical framework has been developed across prior works (Katayama, 2025–2026), this paper deliberately focuses on what remains unresolved. title: V=N/D as Civilizational Metric: Measuring Progress Beyond GDP
abstract: This paper proposes V=N/D — Value equals meaningful action density divided by friction — as a civilizational metric superior to GDP for measuring genuine human progress. GDP measures the volume of economic transactions without regard to their quality, meaning, or friction cost. V=N/D measures the density of meaningful action per unit of friction expended. A civilization that maximizes V is one that produces maximum meaning with minimum effort — the direction of all genuine technological and moral progress.

title: Universal Synchronization Constant (USC):
abstract: The Cosmic Resonance Index (CRI) measures the synchronization between an individual's biorhythm and local high-energy neutrino events (IceCube GOLD-class). While CRI captures individual-cosmic resonance at the scale of blazar jets, it remains a *local* measurement — one instrument listening to one frequency of the universe.  This paper proposes the **Universal Synchronization Constant (USC)**: a framework that expands the scale of measurement from individual ↔ local astrophysical source, to *all life* ↔ *entire universe*.  USC integrates: 1. The Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) — the echo of the Big Bang, pervading all life 2. The Cosmic Neutrino Background (CNB) — the oldest particle signal in existence 3. The baryonic fraction — the 4.9% of the universe that biological life can detect 4
